title: Find north with a stick and its shadow
summary: A reliable method on sunny days, anywhere.
steps: Plant a straight stick in flat ground.
Mark the tip of its shadow with a stone.
Wait 15 to 20 minutes and mark the new tip of the shadow.
Draw a line between the first and second marks: it shows roughly the west (1st mark) – east (2nd mark) axis.
Standing with the 1st mark on your left and the 2nd on your right, you are facing north.

title: Navigating at night by the stars
summary: The North Star in the northern hemisphere, the Southern Cross in the southern hemisphere.
steps: Northern hemisphere: find the Big Dipper (a “saucepan” of 7 stars).
Extend the distance between the two stars on the edge of the pan (opposite the handle) about 5 times.
You reach the North Star (Polaris): it shows north.
Southern hemisphere: extend the long axis of the Southern Cross about 4.5 times its length; south lies straight below that point.

title: Using an analogue watch as a compass
summary: A quick estimate of the direction of south.
steps: Northern hemisphere: point the hour hand at the sun.
The line halfway between the hour hand and 12 points south (use 1 o'clock in summer time).
Southern hemisphere: point 12 at the sun; the line halfway between 12 and the hour hand points north.
warnings: An approximate method, less accurate the closer you are to the equator.

title: Using a compass and a paper map
summary: The basics for following a bearing without GPS.
steps: Orient the map: lay the compass on it and turn the map until its north matches the needle.
To follow a bearing: point the compass's direction-of-travel arrow at the destination, then turn the dial to line up the orienting arrow with the needle.
Keep the needle aligned and walk towards a visible landmark on that line, then repeat.
Keep the compass away from metal objects and phones.
tips: A paper map of your area and a compass belong in your emergency kit.

title: Estimate the time left before nightfall
summary: With your hand held out towards the horizon.
steps: Hold your arm out, hand flat, fingers together and horizontal.
Put the bottom of your hand on the horizon and count how many finger-widths fit up to the sun.
Each finger is about 15 minutes before sunset (4 fingers ≈ 1 hour).
Plan to set up your shelter before the last hour.
warnings: Never look directly at the sun.
